newsitem.title: UK: UK Central Trains seeks 200 voluntary job cuts.
newsitem.headline: UK Central Trains seeks 200 voluntary job cuts.

text.p: Central Trains, the privatised UK passenger rail franchise owned by transport giant National Express Plc, said on Tuesday it was planning 200 voluntary redundancies as part of its cost cutting drive, but denied reports that the cuts could be as high as 1,000 jobs.

A spokesman for Central Trains told Reuters the 1,000 job loss figure cited by railway pressure group Save Our Railways was wrong. But he said "We are seeking 200 voluntary redunancies at our head-office in Birmingham."
He added that the job cuts would effect white collar staff and not train drivers.
Since taking over the rail franchise, Central has cut around 80 jobs, some of which were voluntary. The rail franchise has 2,500 employees in total.
